# Make game audio respond to the world

> AudioPhysx brings purposeful playback tools, physically inspired audio processing and world-aware Blueprint helpers into Unreal Engine. Build sound that reacts to distance, materials, motion and player actions—without turning every MetaSound into a maze of wiring.

- [Make game audio respond to the world](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/readme.md): Make game audio respond to the world
- [Start creating with AudioPhysx](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/getting-started/readme.md): You do not need to understand sound propagation or C++ before getting value from AudioPhysx. Begin with a simple Wave Player and add complexity only when the sound actually calls for it.
- [MetaSound node library](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/metasound/readme.md): AudioPhysx extends MetaSounds with native C++ nodes for playing, processing and controlling sound. Choosing the right category is easier when you begin with the question you want your audio to answer.
- [Connecting game events to audio](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/blueprint/readme.md): MetaSound processes audio, but it does not automatically know where the player is standing, what material a bullet passed, or whether a source is behind a wall.
- [Learn by building something audible](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/examples/readme.md): Every recipe here starts with a sound-design goal, not a list of API calls. You can follow a short graph, listen for a specific result, and then explore the deeper node reference when you want more control.
- [Support, compatibility and updates](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/support/readme.md): Most AudioPhysx issues fall into three groups: a node was not installed or registered correctly; a playback graph has missing triggers or Wave Assets; or a world-driven node receives data in the wrong units or order.

## Getting started

- [Before you begin](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/getting-started/requirements.md): AudioPhysx is a native Unreal Engine C++ plugin. This documentation currently reflects a development build for UE 5.8.4; confirm the final supported engine versions on Compatibility before installing a commercial package.
- [Installing AudioPhysx](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/getting-started/installation.md): The exact steps depend on whether you're using a Fab-distributed plugin or a source checkout. Choose the relevant path below. In either case, the first goal is to see the AudioPhysx node categories in the MetaSound editor.
- [Your first AudioPhysx MetaSound](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/getting-started/first-metasound.md): We're going to create a sound that has three distinct stages: a click, a mechanical movement, and a final clunk. One Play trigger starts the action; AudioPhysx waits for each recording to finish before moving to the next.
- [Signals, events and the end of a sound](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/getting-started/signals-and-completion.md): Many AudioPhysx graph problems aren't about decoding audio; they're about confusing an event, an audio stream, and a lifecycle signal. Understanding these three concepts will make every node easier to use.
- [Quick setup checklist](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/getting-started/checklist.md): Use this before assuming a node is broken. It catches the most common installation, routing and completion mistakes.

## MetaSound nodes

- [Playback — choose the right player](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/metasound/playback.md): Playback nodes select, schedule and combine recordings. Use them when a sound needs a behaviour more involved than simply playing one Wave Asset when it receives a trigger.
- [Acoustics — change the character of sound](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/metasound/acoustics.md): These nodes are for effects that can make the same recording behave differently in different spaces, behind different materials or at different listener positions.
- [Propagation — distance and motion](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/metasound/propagation.md): When we see an explosion far away, the light arrives almost immediately while the sound takes time. A moving vehicle can change the apparent pitch and travel time of its sound.
- [QoL — small controls that clean up large graphs](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/metasound/qol.md): These nodes deal mainly with events and numbers, not audio samples. Their purpose is to replace common branches, random checks and smoothing networks that would otherwise appear in every MetaSound.
- [Passing world data into MetaSound](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/metasound/interfaces.md): A Wave Player can play a recording with only a trigger, but an acoustic processor needs to know something about the world: distance, material, obstruction, source direction or environment.

- [Acoustics reference](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/metasound/nodes/acoustics/readme.md): These processors shape mono audio using material, route, orientation or impact information.

#### Propagation node reference

- [Propagation reference](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/metasound/nodes/propagation/readme.md): These tools work with sound travel time, atmosphere and source-listener movement.
- [AP: Atmosphere Absorption](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/metasound/nodes/propagation/atmosphere-absorption.md): MetaSound · AudioPhysx / Propagation

#### QoL node reference

- [QoL reference](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/metasound/nodes/qol/readme.md): These utilities help manage triggers and smooth the values feeding other nodes.

- [AP: Float Smoother](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/metasound/nodes/qol/float-smoother.md): MetaSound · AudioPhysx / Qol

## Blueprint integration

- [Projectile flybys from Blueprint](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/blueprint/flyby.md): A good near-miss sound is about where the projectile passed and when the listener would hear it, not simply whether the weapon fired. AudioPhysx lets you
- [Playback helpers from Blueprint](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/blueprint/playback-helpers.md): You don't need a dedicated audio Actor to use every AudioPhysx feature. The public Blueprint library provides convenient entry points for sounds at world locations and for registering existing audio components with the plugin's managed update system.
- [Querying acoustic paths](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/blueprint/acoustic-paths.md): A direct ray between a speaker and listener may cross a barrier. In some scenes, sound could instead travel through an opening or around an obstacle. AudioPhysx's path solver provides a game-thread approximation of that situation, producing an acoustic route that the MetaSound can render.
- [Representing an acoustic scene](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/blueprint/components.md): AudioPhysx has components that connect real game objects to the acoustic model. You don't need all of them for ordinary playback. They're most useful when you want source-to-listener obstruction or around-opening behaviour to react to the level.
- [Acoustic Physical Materials](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/blueprint/materials-and-settings.md): An acoustic material describes how an authored surface should affect sound. It is not a recording and is not automatically measured from your level geometry.

## Examples and recipes

- [A one-shot that doesn't sound identical every time](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/examples/randomized-one-shot.md): Goal: Make footsteps, impacts or small interactions feel less repetitive by varying the recording instead of triggering one identical file on every event.
- [Automatic weapon sound with RPM](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/examples/automatic-weapon.md): Goal: Start a weapon with an attack recording, repeat variable shot bodies at an actual firing rate, and play a proper release tail when the player lets go of the trigger.
- [One action, several random stages](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/examples/random-sequence.md): Goal: Keep the order of a sound effect recognizable while allowing its individual details to change.
- [Footsteps that match the ground](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/examples/material-footsteps.md): Goal: Make a footstep choose the correct texture—stone, grass, metal or another material—based on what the player actually stepped on.
- [A projectile passing close to the listener](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/examples/projectile-flyby.md): Goal: Hear an appropriate flyby when a projectile passes nearby, without playing a near-miss sound for every shot in the level.
- [Make a sound believable behind a wall](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/examples/acoustic-obstruction.md): Goal: Have a mono sound change its tone and apparent arrival when the path between source and listener becomes obstructed.

## Support and reference

- [Troubleshooting AudioPhysx](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/support/troubleshooting.md): When something goes wrong, isolate the system in this order: can Unreal play the asset? → does the MetaSound receive a trigger? → does the node output audio?
- [Frequently asked questions](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/support/faq.md): No. It provides additional C++ nodes and Blueprint integration for the existing Unreal audio pipeline. You still use MetaSound Sources, the mixer, spatialization, Sound Attenuation and concurrency features as appropriate for your game.
- [Engine and platform compatibility](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/support/compatibility.md): A plugin is only supported where its exact distributable build has been compiled, loaded and tested. The current docs reflect the UE 5.8.4 development source reviewed on 27 November 2026; the final Fab release package has not yet passed a complete independently verified matrix.
- [Version history](https://DaSypher.github.io/AudioPhysx-Docs/support/changelog.md): The documentation was expanded into a practical learning site, including individual explanations for the existing MetaSound nodes, Blueprint guides, example workflows and a screenshot plan.
